messages:
Alex: Quick sync — attaching the weekly GPU capacity snapshot and a short risk callout. Main points: US-WEST is ~92% committed for next 72h with two queued canaries; EU-CENTRAL shows growing queue pressure due to maintenance windows in the zone (egress throttles), APAC-SG has spare reserved capacity but we expect spike Thursday from a partner test. Link to dashboard: <https://dash.redwood.internal/capacity/weekly|weekly capacity dashboard> :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Maya: Thanks. Can you paste the 72h numbers here? need to tell support about pre-warm windows.

Alex: Sure — quick table:
- US-WEST: projected GPU hours 72h = 18,400h, committed = 16,900h, headroom = 1,500h (8%); runway w/ current autoscale = ~30h for tail loads
- EU-CENTRAL: projected = 9,200h, committed = 8,400h, headroom = 800h (9%); note: egress maintenance 03:00-07:00 UTC Tue/Wed reduces effective throughput by ~15%
- APAC-SG: projected = 6,800h, committed = 4,200h, headroom = 2,600h (38%); partner test Thu expected +1,600h spike

Priya: Heads up — the APAC partner test was only scoped for 800h last week. If it's 1,600h we should reserve a burst pool or route some jobs to US-WEST overnight.

Liam: Is there any chance to shift low-priority batches to APAC to free US-WEST? We can also preempt noncritical jobs during the surge window.

Sam: Cost note — shifting to on-demand in US-WEST for extra 1,500h over the week adds ~30% unit cost vs reserved capacity. If we can route 800h to APAC (reserved) we save ~24k USD.

Alex: Agreed. Proposed actions: 1) Pre-warm 10 nodes in APAC Wed 22:00 local (to hit partner SLA). 2) Apply temporary routing rule: low-priority label -> prefer APAC between 00:00-10:00 UTC. 3) Short-term quantization rollouts to reduce token CPU on non-chat jobs.

Maya: I'll schedule the pre-warm. Quick command I'll run:
```bash
# prewarm nodes in apac pool
infractl pool prewarm --region apac-sg --count 10 --reason "partner test"
```

Priya: Re routing — please add a canary with sticky routing for 1 hour before full toggle, so we can validate latency/SLO. Also add a regression alert on model quality.

Alex: Good call. We'll do 1-hour canary. Config snippet for the canary: 
```yaml
route: low-priority -> apac-prefer-canary
canary:
  duration: 1h
  traffic: 5%
  fallback: us-west
```

Liam: On EU egress — ops-bot reported an upcoming NIC firmware update in eu-c zone. If that hits during the maintenance window it could cascade. Recommend we reduce concurrent KV cache flushes during 03:00-07:00 UTC.

ops-bot: [alert] eu-c zone firmware maintenance scheduled 2026-02-18T03:00Z - 2026-02-18T07:00Z. Expected transient egress throttling <15%. See <https://infra.incidents/redwood/4567|maintenance ticket>.

Sam: If throttling happens, cost could spike if we fall back to on-demand in neighboring regions. Estimate worst-case add-on = 9k USD for the window. Need leadership OK to consume that if we must.

Alex: I'll loop in product to approve fallback spend threshold. @Priya can you own the routing canary and post results by 10:30 UTC Thu?

Priya: Yep — I'll instrument latency and 95/99 token cost. Will post summary and a quick perf diff.

Maya: Pre-warm scheduled, canary config pushed to staging. I'll post the job IDs when pre-warm is live.

deploy-bot: Deployment started: canary-route apac-prefer-canary by Alex at 2026-02-16T18:12:03Z.

Alex: Thanks all. TL;DR: US-WEST tight but manageable, APAC to absorb partner spike with pre-warm, EU has a small egress risk during maintenance window — monitor and be ready to activate fallbacks. I'll update the dashboard after the canary and post the final numbers in tomorrow's follow-up. :thumbsup:
